doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

title: Elvis, 'the Baron' and mother's views on music and money
summary: Cutting school for Elvis movies, early session earnings, his father's nickname, and his mother's remark about the studio.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That's great. This has really been a fascinating chat. And I wanted to ask you two things that I read and we'll wrap it up. It said that you used to cut school to go watch Elvis Presley movies.

Loved him. Learned how to play the guitar as a kid, a real kid dirt young. And I learned how to — my mother used to say in that rough neighborhood where we grew up, she used to say, "You could go into a bar and probably make more money than I made in the store today."
Yes it reminds me of some of the guys that played in the Depression. Eddie [Billy] Bauer talked about making, you know 40 bucks a week when his father was making 8.
That's right. My father used to call me "the Baron."

When I would have a few sessions in the week at age 13 or 14. And I'd come home in a herringbone coat because Curtis you had to dress up for anyway. You had to wear a suit and tie at Curtis. So but yeah, my dad at one time called me "the Baron."

But when they saw that I built this studio my mother went, "Oy my God." She plotzed. She said, "Isn't this too big?" Then she said, her big phrase to me was, "Somehow you got music and money too intermingled."
How could that possibly happen? You did what you loved man that's saying a lot.
